approach: Fix group construction in `Plan::build_with`. The wave loop keeps choosing items in the existing order: best effective priority among ready items, then rung, then age. It stops grouping items itself and only appends the wave's sorted ids to `plan.order`. After the loop, a new private helper `groups_in_order` builds `plan.groups` from `plan.order`, taking items in plan order. An item joins the current last group only when it is `disjoint()` with every member and depends on none of them. Otherwise it starts a new group. Joining only the last group is what lets an item land in the earliest group after its dependencies while keeping the flattened groups equal to `order`. A lower-priority item can then never slip into a group ahead of a higher-priority item it clashes with, and with one job at a time drain dispatches exactly in plan order. The `build_improving` regrouping is left as it is: it splits the new groups around a moved item and still flattens to the moved order. `batches_for` stays a filter. Docs in `plan.rs` and `drain.rs` are updated, as are the existing group tests whose expectations the new rule changes. New tests are added in `plan.rs` and `drain.rs`, plus a `CHANGELOG.md` entry.

decisions.choice: Build groups in a separate pass over `plan.order`. An item joins only the last group, when it is `disjoint()` with all members and depends on none of them. Otherwise it opens a new group.
decisions.reason: The brief wants an item to join the earliest group after its dependencies, in plan order, and also wants drain to dispatch exactly in plan order. Both hold only if no item is placed ahead of an earlier-ordered item it could not join. Since deps always sit earlier in the order, 'earliest legal group' reduces to 'the last group, if no dependency is in it'. Flattened groups then equal `order` by construction, and `batches_for` needs no change.

rejected.option: Literal 'earliest group after deps where disjoint', searching all existing groups, then deriving `order` from the groups
rejected.why: Say u1 and u2 clash and n is disjoint. n would join u1's group ahead of u2. That is exactly today's fault: a lower-priority item dispatches before a higher-priority one.
Treats the symptom. `athena plan` would still print groups that disagree with the order, and the user default is to fix group construction.

rejected.option: Keep each wave as a group boundary, so a group never spans two effective-priority waves
rejected.why: The brief says dependencies are the only barrier ('earliest group after everything it depends on'). Wave boundaries would also keep disjoint urgent and normal items from running side by side when max_concurrency is above 1.

decisions.choice: `order` becomes the wave's (rung, age)-sorted list. It is no longer the concatenation of greedy groups. Nothing else about the wave selection changes: best effective priority among ready items, then rung, then age.
decisions.reason: The greedy grouping was reshuffling the wave's items. A disjoint later item could join an early group and run before an earlier clashing item of its own wave. Making the plan order the sorted wave removes that, and groups are derived from it.

rejected.option: Add own priority as a within-wave tiebreak, so urgent items precede a normal dependency raised to urgent
rejected.why: It changes the ordering rules, which the brief puts out of scope. The dependency reason already covers a raised item sitting ahead of its dependents' peers.

decisions.choice: Leave the `build_improving` regrouping (plan.rs ~L928-943) unchanged. Add an assertion that the flattened groups equal the moved order.
decisions.reason: It splits groups around a moved improvement request, and its input groups now flatten to the original order. Each old group still sits wholly before the groups holding its dependents, so the dependency rule holds. The brief says to keep it consistent, not to redesign it.

rejected.option: Rebuild groups from the moved order with `groups_in_order`, then force moved items into singletons
rejected.why: More change for the same result, and it risks the 'moved request is a group of its own' guarantee.

steps: plan.rs: in `build_with`, replace the greedy per-wave grouping with `for (_, e) in &ready { plan.order.push(e.id.clone()); }`, leaving the ready/best-priority/(rung, age) selection and the `done` bookkeeping untouched.

plan.rs: add private `fn groups_in_order(order: &[String], planned: &[&PlanEntry]) -> Vec<Vec<String>>`. For each id in order, find its entry (skip any with none). If the last group exists, every member is `disjoint(member, entry)` and none is in `entry.depends_on`, push into the last group. Otherwise start a new group. Set `plan.groups = groups_in_order(&plan.order, &planned)` after the loop. `planned` is the vector of retained pending entries built before the loop. Cyclic items are not in `order`, so they are not grouped.

CHANGELOG.md: under `## [Unreleased]`, add an entry in the section the file uses for fixes (add `### Fixed` if the section is missing). It says: `athena drain` now dispatches in `athena plan`'s order when groups are involved. The plan built groups per wave by greedy joining, so a lower-priority item could sit in an earlier group than a higher-priority one that clashed with an earlier item, and drain, which works groups in sequence, started it first. Groups are now built from the plan order — each item joins the last group if it is path-disjoint and independent, otherwise it opens a new group, so a group is always after its dependencies — and flattened groups equal the order. State the effect on parallel group shape.
Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`.

risks.risk: Cross-priority joins: a lower-priority disjoint item can now share a group with a higher-priority one that precedes it, because waves no longer bound groups. With max_concurrency above 1 they run side by side.
risks.mitigation: This is the stated rule ('earliest group after everything it depends on'). Groups are still path-disjoint and dependency-free, which is all the parallel scheduler and landing check rely on. The only visible changes are the `athena plan` group lines and some group sizes. The plan lists each existing group assertion, and the producer runs the full `cargo test --locked`.

risks.risk: Less parallelism in the clash case. An item that clashes with an earlier one now starts a new group, and later disjoint items join that group instead of the earliest one.
risks.mitigation: Under the new rule, rung and age order sets the plan order within a wave, so an item that clashes with an earlier one waits instead of being passed by later disjoint items. Breadth on realistic plans is mostly unchanged ([3,1,2] sizes stay the same), but a clash chain can now give narrower groups. The trade-off is documented in the `build_with` doc.

risks.risk: The brief's literal case (normal plus urgent, disjoint, no dependency) already orders correctly in the old wave loop, so on its own it would not show the fix.
risks.mitigation: The criterion-1 test (b) and the criterion-3 test pin the incident shape (clashing urgent items plus a normal dependency of an urgent item), which fails on the old code. Test (a) is kept as the brief's literal case and as a guard.

risks.risk: The improvement-turn move can still put a normal Steward request ahead of urgent items. That is by design, not a regression.
risks.mitigation: Left unchanged by design (out of scope). The existing tests assert it, and `priority_violations` already exempts moved items. The new flatten == order assertions run over `build_improving` output.

demonstrations.method: Add two unit tests in the `tests` module of drain.rs. Test (a) queues a normal item n first, then an urgent item u, with disjoint touched paths and no dependency. It runs `drain_concurrent(&world, limits(20.0), &Quiet, 1)` and asserts the `start` entries in the log are [u, n], and that `Plan::build` groups flatten to the same order. Test (b) is the incident shape described above, with 1 worker, and asserts the start order.
demonstrations.observes: Starts follow plan order, with the urgent item first in (a) and [u1,u2,n,u3,u4] in (b). The report stop is `QueueEmpty`.
demonstrations.fails_without: Test (a), the brief's normal plus urgent pair, is a regression guard and may already pass before the change. Test (b) uses the shape from the 2026-10-27 report. u1 and u2 share a path, n is a normal dependency of urgent u4, and u3 is urgent. The old greedy grouping starts u1, n, u3, u2, u4, so (b) fails there. The test expects u1, u2, n, u3, u4.

demonstrations.method: Add a unit test in plan.rs `tests`. It builds `Plan::build` for three cases, each with an unrelated disjoint item. (i) A normal base with an urgent dependent. (ii) An urgent base with a low dependent. (iii) A high dependent of a normal base alongside an urgent unrelated item. For each case it asserts the base's group index is less than the dependent's, and that the base precedes the dependent in `order`.
demonstrations.observes: The group-index and order comparisons hold in all three cases.

demonstrations.method: Add a unit test in plan.rs. The mixed plan is: urgent u1 and u2 on the same path, normal n that urgent u4 depends on, urgent u3, plus a high item, a low item and a normal item on other paths and rungs. It builds `Plan::build`, then `Plan::build_capped` and `Plan::build_improving`. It asserts `groups.concat() == order` for each. For every earlier x and later y with y's own priority better than x's, it asserts that x is a transitive dependency of an item at least as urgent as y. A small test-local helper walks `depends_on` to check this. It also asserts `priority_violations(&entries)` is empty and pins the exact order and groups for the incident shape.
demonstrations.observes: Flattened groups equal the order in all three builders, no unexplained priority inversion exists, and the exact order and groups match.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the old greedy grouping, the exact assertions fail on this mixed plan. Old groups are [[u1,n,u3],[u2],[u4]] and the old order is u1,n,u3,u2,u4. The expected order is [u1,u2,n,u3,u4] and the expected groups are [[u1],[u2,n,u3],[u4]]. The fault also shows if the joining pass is changed to search earlier groups.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `Plan::build`, `Plan::build_capped` and `Plan::build_improving`. The plan.rs `tests` helpers `entry`, `with_priority` and `improvement` supply the entries. No double is used. The seam exists; `groups_in_order` is added by step 1.
